title: Flat and Apartment Buying Legal Checklist in Bangladesh 2026: Registration Fees, Developer Disputes & Gain Tax
metaTitle: Flat & Apartment Buying Legal Checklist Bangladesh 2026: Fees & Laws
metaDescription: Essential legal checklist before buying an apartment in Dhaka. Real Estate Act 2010 safeguards, flat registration cost breakdown, Gain Tax (AIT), and developer dispute remedies.

heroIntro: Purchasing a flat or apartment in Dhaka—whether in Uttara, Mirpur, Bashundhara, Dhanmondi, or Gulshan—represents one of the largest capital investments an individual or expatriate family will ever make. However, the urban real estate market is fraught with perils: developer delivery delays spanning years, unapproved floor additions violating RAJUK master plans, mortgaged mother land, and staggering hidden registration and tax costs. The Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010 (রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়ন ও ব্যবস্থাপনা আইন ২০১০) grants robust statutory rights to apartment buyers, provided the contractual documents are drafted and vetted with absolute precision. This definitive 2026 guide by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, provides the ultimate buyer's legal checklist.

quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ Apartment Purchase Due Diligence & Cost Breakdown 2026
points: Total Registration Burden: Typically 7% to 10% of total recorded deed value (Stamp Duty 1.5%, Registration Fee 1%, Local Govt Tax 1.5–2%, Advance Income Tax / Gain Tax per sq metre).
Developer Mandatory Clearances: Verify RAJUK/CDA structural plan approval, Landowner-Developer Joint Venture Agreement, and Registered Irrevocable Power of Attorney.
Title Due Diligence: Inspect 25–30 year chain deeds (Baya Dalil), CS/SA/RS/City Survey Khatians, and 12-year Sub-Registry Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC).
Real Estate Act 2010 Protection: Developers cannot alter layout plans without written consent, and must compensate buyers for handover delays beyond the contractual deadline.
Professional Legal Vetting: Consult Supreme Court Property Advocate Md. Shah Alam at +8801712655546 before signing the Baina Agreement or paying earnest money.

sections.h2: Why Independent Legal Due Diligence is Vital for Flat Buyers
sections.content: Never rely on a real estate developer’s in-house panel lawyer. In-house lawyers represent the developer's corporate interests, not the buyer's financial safety. An independent property advocate scrutinizes whether the developer has actual authority to sell the flat, whether the landowner has raised any disputes, and whether the project sits on encumbered or mortgaged soil.

sections.h2: Phase 1: Mother Land Title & Survey Verification
sections.content:
An apartment building stands upon 'Mother Land'. If the mother land's title is flawed, every apartment deed constructed upon it is legally compromised:

  • Chain of Ownership (বায়া দলিল): Verify an unbroken 25-to-30-year chain of title connecting current landowners to historical cadastral records.
  • Survey Khatians: Inspect CS, SA, RS, and BS/City Jarip Khatians to ensure the land classification permits residential construction (not wetland/viti or acquired government property).
  • Sub-Registry Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC): Obtain a 12-to-30-year NEC certifying that the landowner has not mortgaged the plot to commercial banks.

sections.h2: Phase 2: Verifying RAJUK, CDA & Municipal Approvals
sections.content:
Unapproved construction is subject to immediate demolition by regulatory authorities:

  • Approved Building Plan (নকশা অনুমোদন): Cross-check the architectural design approved by RAJUK (Dhaka), CDA (Chittagong), or KDA (Khulna).
  • Floor Number Verification: Confirm that the specific flat you are buying is part of the approved floor plan (e.g., buying 8th floor when approval was granted only up to 6 floors is illegal).
  • Fire, Environmental & Civil Aviation NOCs: Ensure high-rise buildings possess valid clearances from the Fire Service and Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB).

sections.h2: Phase 3: The Developer Agreement & Registered Power of Attorney
sections.content:
In joint-venture developments between a private landowner and a developer company:

  1. Examine the Development Agreement (JV Agreement) to see the exact allocation of floors and car parking spaces between landowner and developer.
  2. Verify the Registered Irrevocable General Power of Attorney (IGPA) granted by the landowner to the developer under the Power of Attorney Act 2012, confirming the developer has explicit legal authority to execute sale deeds and accept payments from buyers.

sections.h2: Phase 4: Scrutinizing the Deed of Agreement for Sale (Baina Nama)
sections.content:
The Baina Nama governs the entire transaction until final registration. Ensure these mandatory clauses are included:

  • Exact Specifications: Clear net square footage, common area allocation percentage, and designated car parking slot number.
  • Strict Handover Date & Grace Period: Exact calendar date of flat delivery and compensation penalties for developer delays.
  • No Alteration Clause: A covenant prohibiting the developer from altering architectural layouts without the buyer's written approval.

sections.h2: Apartment Registration Fees & Gain Tax Breakdown (2026 Rates)
sections.content:
The total government cost for registering an apartment in Bangladesh generally amounts to 7% to 10% of the deed valuation:

Tax / Fee Head Applicable Rate (2026)
Stamp Duty 1.5% of total deed value
Registration Fee 1% of deed value
Local Government Tax 1.5% to 2% (City Corporation / Cantonment)
Advance Income Tax (AIT / Gain Tax) Fixed rate per sq metre (Sec 124 of Income Tax Act 2023)

sections.h2: Remedies Under Real Estate Act 2010 for Developer Default
sections.content:
Under the Real Estate Development and Management Act 2010, buyers have robust legal protections:

  • Delay Penalty (Section 15): If the developer fails to deliver the flat within the agreed deadline, they must pay monthly compensation to the buyer at the prescribed statutory rate.
  • Arbitration & Notice: Serving a 30-day statutory legal notice followed by arbitration before the Real Estate Arbitration Board.
  • Criminal Prosecution: Section 27 to 36 impose imprisonment of up to 3 years and heavy fines for developers who defraud buyers, construct unauthorized floors, or pledge allocated apartments to third parties.

sections.h2: Post-Handover Checklist: Mutation, Association & Utility Demarcation
sections.content:
After taking physical possession and executing the final registered sale deed (সাব-কবালা দলিল):

  1. Apply for e-Mutation to record your undivided proportionate land share (অবিভক্ত ও অচিহ্নিত অংশ) in your own name at the local AC Land office.
  2. Transfer DESCO/DPDC electricity meters and Titas Gas connections to your name.
  3. Form the Apartment Owners' Welfare Association to manage common facilities, elevators, and security funds.

faqs.question: Can a developer sell parking spaces separately?
faqs.answer: Under the Real Estate Act 2010, developers cannot sell common areas or open spaces, but designated covered car parking spaces allocated in the approved plan may be allotted to flat buyers.

faqs.question: What is an undivided proportionate land share?
faqs.answer: When you buy an apartment, you own both the physical flat space and a proportionate undivided ownership share of the land underneath the building.

faqs.question: What should I do if a developer delays apartment handover?
faqs.answer: Serve a formal legal notice through a Supreme Court advocate demanding completion and monthly financial compensation under Section 15 of the Real Estate Act 2010, followed by an arbitration claim or criminal complaint.
